skill.name: page-cro
skill.description: Analyze marketing pages for conversion problems and recommend clear CRO improvements for copy, CTAs, layout, trust signals, and tests.
skill.summary: Reviews marketing pages and produces prioritized conversion optimization recommendations.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

security_audit.summary: Reviewed the three static system-reconnaissance flags in SKILL.md. They are benign CRO references to landing pages, paid ads, and layout tests, not host or network reconnaissance. No prompt injection, exfiltration, network access, or tool abuse was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Test grid vs. list view layouts

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 16 lists landing pages as a marketing page type for CRO review. It does not request host discovery, network scanning, or sensitive system information.
Line 34 asks about paid ad messaging as traffic context for marketing analysis. This is ordinary campaign context, not system reconnaissance.
Line 311 suggests testing grid versus list layouts for a resource page. This is a visual layout experiment and has no system or security reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Marketing pages often lose visitors through unclear messaging, weak CTAs, or missing trust signals. This skill reviews page structure and gives prioritized CRO recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Identifies page type, primary conversion goal, and traffic context before giving recommendations.
Reviews value proposition, headline clarity, CTAs, visual hierarchy, trust signals, objections, and friction points.
Organizes recommendations into quick wins, high-impact changes, test ideas, and copy alternatives.
Applies separate CRO guidance for homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, and blog posts.
Suggests experiment ideas for hero sections, social proof, navigation, pricing, forms, and resource sections.
limitations: It cannot measure live conversion rates unless the user provides analytics data.
It does not implement page changes or run A/B tests by itself.
Recommendation quality depends on the page copy, screenshots, goals, and traffic context provided.
It is not focused on signup flows, onboarding, standalone forms, or popup optimization.

use_cases.title: Audit a Campaign Landing Page
use_cases.description: Review message match, CTA focus, trust signals, and friction before paid traffic scales.

use_cases.title: Improve a Pricing Page
use_cases.description: Find plan comparison issues, pricing objections, and conversion barriers for high-intent visitors.

use_cases.title: Convert Blog Traffic
use_cases.description: Add contextual CTAs, lead magnets, and resource paths that fit article intent.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Page Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first CRO pass.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this marketing page for conversion problems. Focus on the headline, CTA, trust signals, and the top three quick wins.

prompt_templates.title: Landing Page CRO Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for paid campaign traffic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this landing page for paid traffic. Check message match, one primary CTA, above-the-fold clarity, objections, and friction points.

prompt_templates.title: Pricing Page Optimization
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for a SaaS pricing page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this pricing page. Identify plan comparison issues, value clarity gaps, trust signals, and tests that could improve paid conversions.

prompt_templates.title: CRO Experiment Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a conversion testing program.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a CRO roadmap for this page. Prioritize quick wins, high-impact changes, A/B test hypotheses, copy alternatives, and success metrics.

output_examples.input: A homepage has a vague headline, two competing primary buttons, and no visible social proof.
output_examples.output: The review highlights unclear positioning, CTA conflict, and missing trust signals. It recommends a specific benefit-led headline, one primary CTA, and proof near the hero section.

output_examples.input: A pricing page shows four plans, hides annual savings, and uses generic buttons.
output_examples.output: The review recommends a clearer plan hierarchy, visible annual savings, stronger CTA copy, pricing FAQs, and a test for highlighting the recommended plan.

output_examples.input: A blog post attracts search traffic but has only one CTA at the end.
output_examples.output: The review suggests inline CTAs, a topic-matched lead magnet, related resources, and an exit path that fits the reader intent.

best_practices: Provide the page goal, audience, traffic source, and current conversion rate when available.
Share screenshots or page copy so the review can evaluate hierarchy and messaging accurately.
Treat test ideas as hypotheses and validate them with clean experiment design.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for generic CRO tips without page context or a clear conversion goal.
Do not apply every recommendation at once when you need reliable test results.
Do not use this skill for security reviews, analytics instrumentation, or backend performance debugging.

faq.question: What pages does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews homepages, landing pages, pricing pages, feature pages, blog posts, resource pages, and demo request pages.

faq.question: Can it write new page copy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can provide headline, CTA, value proposition, and section copy alternatives with rationale.

faq.question: Does it replace analytics tools?
faq.answer: No. It uses provided analytics context but does not collect data or measure conversions directly.

faq.question: Can it create A/B test ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests hypotheses for page elements such as headlines, CTAs, social proof, navigation, pricing, and forms.

faq.question: Is this skill for signup form optimization?
faq.answer: No. It points users to related signup-flow, onboarding, form, or popup CRO skills for those focused workflows.

faq.question: What input gives the best result?
faq.answer: Provide the page URL or copy, screenshots, audience, traffic source, conversion goal, and known performance data.
